sections.skill: Build an email list with permission and follow opt-out rules

questions.domain: Foundation 11: Marketing, sales and social media
questions.prompt: How should an email list be built?

choices.text: By copying addresses from other companies' websites
By buying a list of strangers' addresses online
With permission, through a sign-up form
By guessing addresses at popular email providers

questions.correct_answer: With permission, through a sign-up form
questions.intro: An EMAIL LIST lets you contact people who asked to hear from you. Build it with PERMISSION: a sign-up form where people choose to join. Under the US CAN-SPAM Act, commercial emails must not use misleading headers or subject lines, must tell recipients how to opt out, must honor opt-out requests, and must include a valid physical postal address (which can be a registered PO Box or private mailbox). The rules cover business-to-business email too. Buying lists of strangers' addresses damages trust and deliverability.

questions.prompt: An email list is like what?

choices.text: A guest list of people who said yes

questions.correct_answer: A guest list of people who said yes
questions.intro: Think of a party. People you invited are glad to come. People who show up uninvited annoy everyone. An email list is your guest list: people who said "yes, invite me." When a guest says "please stop inviting me," you take them off the list. Sending emails to people who never signed up is like inviting gate-crashers.
